correctness.rationale: In K[D₂ₙ]=R⊕Rs, right multiplication by 1+r+s sends (u,v) to ((1+r)u+v,u+(1+r⁻¹)v), so v is fixed by u in the kernel and the remaining condition is (1+r+r²)u=0. For a check that does not assume semisimplicity, cyclic coefficients satisfy a three-term recurrence in characteristic two: each next value is the sum of the prior two. Hence the sequence is 3-periodic and is determined by any first two values. If 3 divides n all two-parameter sequences are allowed, even if n is even; otherwise n-periodicity forces a constant sequence and the recurrence forces zero. This verifies the corank over any extension K. In the invertible case the squares are a basis. Multiplying an ideal element by a basis vector first extracts a nonzero multiple of a square, and propagating by the support arcs gets all squares, since r and s generate the group as a monoid. In the singular case the span of the squares is a nonzero proper ideal. Independent squares force any automorphism to have disjoint column supports; invertibility makes it monomial, and comparison at each diagonal coefficient 1 makes every multiplier 1. The unique reciprocal nonloop arc is the s-arc and the other is the r-arc for n≥3. A digraph automorphism therefore commutes with right multiplication by both generators and is exactly a left translation. This proves the full ordinary group, independent of K, in the nonsingular cases only. Reviewed RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and verify.py as text; no attached code executed.
